The molecule that ends vaginal dryness after menopause was discovered in 1934.

Your gynecologist has never once offered it to you.

It BOILS my blood, because I found it by accident after two years of pain.

Once you see what it really is, you'll be as angry as I am.

Your body makes one molecule whose only job is holding water in that tissue. After menopause, it drops by up to 94%.

That's it. That's the whole thing.

The vaginal tissue dries from the inside, thins, and tears at the lightest touch. That's the sandpaper. 

That's the blood on the sheets you've been blaming yourself for. Not aging. One molecule, GONE.

And here's the part that made my throat tight in anger.

That molecule isn't rare. It's called hyaluronic acid, and medicine has used it everywhere for ninety years.

Eye surgeons use it. Knee surgeons inject it. It's in the face cream on your shelf right now. Dentists use it to heal the inside of your mouth.

Everywhere on your body. Except the one place menopause was stripping it from.

Not because it was hard. The molecule was right there. They just decided that once you stopped being able to have kids, the rest of you wasn't worth the trouble. So they handed you a tube and told you to cope. 

That's when I understood why nothing I'd tried before was made to heal, and only made my symptoms worse.

For example, the lube doctors recommend only puts water on top of tissue that's dry from the inside. It's like trying to soak a waterproof jacket.

And I thought I could just use  hyaluronic acid, but that molecule is too big to be absorbed by the vaginal tissue.

That's why you need it in the lesser form: sodium hyaluronate.

And OMG, this article I read made me hold my head, because I could not believe it.

In 2023, sodium hyaluronate went head to head with a $1,500 laser treatment for vaginal dryness.

And guess what?

They both had the same result for the two groups of females… that's how POWERFUL this thing is.

A product that treats the symptom keeps you a subscription and a money machine. That's why they never hand off the thing that actually treats the tissue.

But that ends today\!

After sodium hyaluronate brings water back to the vaginal tissue, it doesn't end there.

Because your tissue is torn and you need something to build it back up, which is why you need Centella. Burn units have used it for centuries to rebuild what got thin enough to bleed.

And this is the part that scared me the most and made me anxious.

If the vaginal wall is left torn and untreated, it lets bad bacteria in, causing BV, yeast infections, and leaving us to live on antibiotics forever\!

And the whole time, the one place menopause was tearing apart got a tube of lube. 

And this is what led me to do more research, to look for a product that actually combines sodium hyaluronate and the other ingredients. 

I looked for one that's hormone-free, because cancer runs in my family. 

One gentle enough for tissue that's already raw. And reaction-free, because my hooha reacts to everything.

So I found a suppository, inserted inside the vagina to target the actual tissue.

Because I knew pills don't work — the stomach acid destroys them before they reach the tissue — and topical creams don't get absorbed.

I spent 22 years treating arthritis. Then at 54, I got it myself.

I did everything I'd told my patients to do — perfectly. And my joints kept getting worse anyway.

That's when I realised I'd been giving people the wrong advice for two decades 👇

Let me explain what almost no one gets told at diagnosis.
Arthritis pain isn't caused by one thing. It's caused by two completely different types of inflammation — and they behave nothing alike.

The FIRST type is the one you feel. The swelling. The heat. The ache that flares when you overdo it and settles when you rest. This is the one everything targets — the painkillers, the gels, the turmeric. It's the loud one.

The SECOND type is the one you can't feel. And it's the dangerous one.

It doesn't cause swelling. It doesn't cause pain. Instead, it quietly releases enzymes that break down your cartilage — the smooth cushion that stops your bones grinding against each other. And here's the part I need you to understand, because it's why people come to me too late:

Cartilage has no nerve endings.

So while this second inflammation is doing the real, permanent damage… you feel absolutely nothing. No warning. No ache telling you to stop. Nothing — right up until the cushion is worn so thin that bone starts touching bone.

THAT is the day the pain "suddenly" arrives. On the stairs. Getting out of the car. And everyone says the same thing: "it came out of nowhere."

It didn't. It had been building silently for years.

Now — let me rank what people actually take for this, worst to best, so you can see the problem clearly.

IBUPROFEN & PAINKILLERS — 2 out of 10.

 They block the pain for about four hours and do nothing to either inflammation. Taken daily for years they wreck your stomach and let the silent damage run completely unchecked. They hide the warning. They don't treat anything.

COLLAGEN — 3 out of 10.

 Lovely for skin and nails. But you cannot rebuild cartilage in a joint that's still actively being broken down. It's laying new carpet in a flooding room.

GLUCOSAMINE — 4 out of 10.

 The one everyone's mother swears by. The research is genuinely mixed and modest at best. Most of my patients take it for three months, feel nothing they can be sure of, and quietly stop.

TURMERIC — 7 out of 10, and this is the important one.

 Because if you took turmeric, your instinct was RIGHT. Real turmeric — standardised to 95% curcumin — is one of the best natural anti-inflammatories we have. But there are two problems. First, most turmeric on the shelf is 3-5% curcumin — a fraction of what you need, and your gut destroys most of that before it reaches the joint. Second, and this is the crucial bit: even perfect turmeric only treats the FIRST inflammation. The one you feel. It barely touches the second one — the one destroying your cartilage.

So turmeric was never wrong.

It was just never finished.

Here's the half you were missing 👇

BOSWELLIA — the missing partner.

 Boswellia is an ancient resin — you might know it as frankincense — and it does the one thing turmeric can't: it acts directly on that second inflammatory pathway, the silent one degrading your cartilage. It's not a replacement for turmeric. It's the other half of it.
Curcumin for the fire you feel.

 Boswellia for the fire you can't.

Together — 9 out of 10. The only combination that actually addresses both types of inflammation at once.

I spent 22 years treating arthritis. Then at 54, I got it myself.

I did everything I'd told my patients to do — perfectly. And my joints kept getting worse anyway.

That's when I realised I'd been giving people the wrong advice for two decades 👇

Let me explain what almost no one gets told at diagnosis.
Arthritis pain isn't caused by one thing. It's caused by two completely different types of inflammation — and they behave nothing alike.

The FIRST type is the one you feel. The swelling. The heat. The ache that flares when you overdo it and settles when you rest. This is the one everything targets — the painkillers, the gels, the turmeric. It's the loud one.

The SECOND type is the one you can't feel. And it's the dangerous one.

It doesn't cause swelling. It doesn't cause pain. Instead, it quietly releases enzymes that break down your cartilage — the smooth cushion that stops your bones grinding against each other. And here's the part I need you to understand, because it's why people come to me too late:

Cartilage has no nerve endings.

So while this second inflammation is doing the real, permanent damage… you feel absolutely nothing. No warning. No ache telling you to stop. Nothing — right up until the cushion is worn so thin that bone starts touching bone.

THAT is the day the pain "suddenly" arrives. On the stairs. Getting out of the car. And everyone says the same thing: "it came out of nowhere."

It didn't. It had been building silently for years.

Now — let me rank what people actually take for this, worst to best, so you can see the problem clearly.

IBUPROFEN & PAINKILLERS — 2 out of 10.

 They block the pain for about four hours and do nothing to either inflammation. Taken daily for years they wreck your stomach and let the silent damage run completely unchecked. They hide the warning. They don't treat anything.

COLLAGEN — 3 out of 10.

 Lovely for skin and nails. But you cannot rebuild cartilage in a joint that's still actively being broken down. It's laying new carpet in a flooding room.

GLUCOSAMINE — 4 out of 10.

 The one everyone's mother swears by. The research is genuinely mixed and modest at best. Most of my patients take it for three months, feel nothing they can be sure of, and quietly stop.

TURMERIC — 7 out of 10, and this is the important one.

 Because if you took turmeric, your instinct was RIGHT. Real turmeric — standardised to 95% curcumin — is one of the best natural anti-inflammatories we have. But there are two problems. First, most turmeric on the shelf is 3-5% curcumin — a fraction of what you need, and your gut destroys most of that before it reaches the joint. Second, and this is the crucial bit: even perfect turmeric only treats the FIRST inflammation. The one you feel. It barely touches the second one — the one destroying your cartilage.

So turmeric was never wrong.

It was just never finished.

Here's the half you were missing 👇

BOSWELLIA — the missing partner.

 Boswellia is an ancient resin — you might know it as frankincense — and it does the one thing turmeric can't: it acts directly on that second inflammatory pathway, the silent one degrading your cartilage. It's not a replacement for turmeric. It's the other half of it.
Curcumin for the fire you feel.

 Boswellia for the fire you can't.

Together — 9 out of 10. The only combination that actually addresses both types of inflammation at once.

And here's the honest reason almost nobody sells them together at proper strength: it's cheaper to sell you half. A weak turmeric with a big label costs a fraction of a properly dosed, two-ingredient formula. So that's what fills the shelves. You weren't failing at treating your arthritis. You were handed half a treatment and left to wonder why it stalled.

When a single powder or pill promises to address almost every area of your health, it’s worth questioning how much it can realistically do for any one of them.

A long ingredient list can look impressive, but more ingredients doesn’t necessarily mean a better formula. There’s only so much you can fit into a scoop or capsule, and trying to include dozens of ingredients can mean there simply isn’t enough room for meaningful amounts of each.

You shouldn’t need to become a nutritionist or spend hours deciphering dosages to choose a good supplement. Instead, look at the bigger picture: Does this product have a clear purpose? Do the ingredients make sense for that purpose? Are the claims realistic?

There is no magic powder that can do everything.

I did everything I'd told my patients to do — perfectly. And my joints kept getting worse anyway.

That's when I realised I'd been giving people the wrong advice for two decades 👇

Let me explain what almost no one gets told at diagnosis.
Arthritis pain isn't caused by one thing. It's caused by two completely different types of inflammation — and they behave nothing alike.

The FIRST type is the one you feel. The swelling. The heat. The ache that flares when you overdo it and settles when you rest. This is the one everything targets — the painkillers, the gels, the turmeric. It's the loud one.

The SECOND type is the one you can't feel. And it's the dangerous one.

It doesn't cause swelling. It doesn't cause pain. Instead, it quietly releases enzymes that break down your cartilage — the smooth cushion that stops your bones grinding against each other. And here's the part I need you to understand, because it's why people come to me too late:

Cartilage has no nerve endings.

So while this second inflammation is doing the real, permanent damage… you feel absolutely nothing. No warning. No ache telling you to stop. Nothing — right up until the cushion is worn so thin that bone starts touching bone.

THAT is the day the pain "suddenly" arrives. On the stairs. Getting out of the car. And everyone says the same thing: "it came out of nowhere."

It didn't. It had been building silently for years.

Now — let me rank what people actually take for this, worst to best, so you can see the problem clearly.

IBUPROFEN & PAINKILLERS — 2 out of 10.

 They block the pain for about four hours and do nothing to either inflammation. Taken daily for years they wreck your stomach and let the silent damage run completely unchecked. They hide the warning. They don't treat anything.

COLLAGEN — 3 out of 10.

 Lovely for skin and nails. But you cannot rebuild cartilage in a joint that's still actively being broken down. It's laying new carpet in a flooding room.

GLUCOSAMINE — 4 out of 10.

 The one everyone's mother swears by. The research is genuinely mixed and modest at best. Most of my patients take it for three months, feel nothing they can be sure of, and quietly stop.

TURMERIC — 7 out of 10, and this is the important one.

 Because if you took turmeric, your instinct was RIGHT. Real turmeric — standardised to 95% curcumin — is one of the best natural anti-inflammatories we have. But there are two problems. First, most turmeric on the shelf is 3-5% curcumin — a fraction of what you need, and your gut destroys most of that before it reaches the joint. Second, and this is the crucial bit: even perfect turmeric only treats the FIRST inflammation. The one you feel. It barely touches the second one — the one destroying your cartilage.

So turmeric was never wrong.

It was just never finished.

Here's the half you were missing 👇

BOSWELLIA — the missing partner.

 Boswellia is an ancient resin — you might know it as frankincense — and it does the one thing turmeric can't: it acts directly on that second inflammatory pathway, the silent one degrading your cartilage. It's not a replacement for turmeric. It's the other half of it.
Curcumin for the fire you feel.

 Boswellia for the fire you can't.

Together — 9 out of 10. The only combination that actually addresses both types of inflammation at once.

And here's the honest reason almost nobody sells them together at proper strength: it's cheaper to sell you half. A weak turmeric with a big label costs a fraction of a properly dosed, two-ingredient formula. So that's what fills the shelves. You weren't failing at treating your arthritis. You were handed half a treatment and left to wonder why it stalled.

✓ 500mg curcumin at 95% (the clinical strength — not the 3% dust)
 ✓ 500mg boswellia (for the second pathway everyone ignores)
 ✓ Black pepper extract (without it, your body flushes the curcumin out before it works)
No fillers. Two capsules in the morning. That's the entire routine.

"Off the ibuprofen I'd taken every day for eleven years." — Margaret, 58
 "Down my own stairs without gripping the rail — first time in two years." — Susan, 61

I'm an OB-GYN. I've had a hysterectomy. And when the things I'd spent twelve years telling women to buy stopped working on me, I sat down and read every label on that shelf.

Here they are, ranked worst to best.

My name is Dr. Chantelle Anderson. Board-certified OB-GYN, 12 years in practice. 
I had my hysterectomy at 45, and within a year I was standing in the same drugstore aisle I'd been sending my own patients to since residency, buying the same products I'd been recommending, with the same result they'd been reporting back to me for over a decade.

Nothing.

So I did the thing I should have done years earlier. I bought the five best-sellers. I read every ingredient list.

And I compared them against what the published literature actually says the problem is.

Three things I want to give you today:

Why almost everything in that aisle fails

The three things nearly every product leaves out

The five that came out on top, in order

Now, here's why almost everything on that shelf fails.

Women assume dryness is a moisture problem. Add moisture, done.

But it isn't. When estrogen drops — gradually in menopause, or overnight if your ovaries came out with your uterus — four things go wrong at once: 

The tissue stops holding water. That's the dryness.

The wall thins. No estrogen, which means no collagen. That's the tearing and the pain.

It gets inflamed. That's the burning on a Tuesday afternoon when nothing's happening.

Your pH climbs from about 4 towards 6. And the more it climbs, the easier it is for E. coli to take hold — which is where the recurrent UTIs come from. And nobody told me that. 

Four problems. All coming from one cause.

Now here's what I found when I read those labels: almost every one treats the first problem only. Moisture. 

Which means the other three — the tissue, the inflammation, and the pH — go untreated. Every product, same three gaps.

Which is why you can successfully treat your dryness and still be burning, still tearing, still on antibiotics twice a year — and conclude that your body is just failing. It isn't. You treated a quarter of the problem.

Women tell me they're drier the day after than they were before. Every week. For twelve years I had no explanation for that.

Then I read the labels.

The ingredient that makes most of these slippery is a water magnet. Once it's inside you, it keeps pulling — from your own tissue.

There's a measure for this. Osmolality. Your tissue sits around 370. The WHO says these products should be under 380.

Testing found them at 2,000. 3,000. Some over 6,000.

That advisory came out in 2012. Nothing on that shelf changed, because nothing had to.

That's the lens I used. Now, here's the list, worst to best.

#5 — K-Y, Astroglide, and every water-based lubricant

I'm including these because they're what most women are handed first, including by physicians. Including by me.

Water and glycerin, essentially. But glycerin's the water magnet. This is the drier-the-next-day problem, in its purest form.

Yes, they do work — for about twenty minutes, at reducing friction during sex, which is the entire job they were designed to do.

Read the front of the box. It says personal lubricant. 

That's not marketing. That's a category, and a lubricant isn't required to do anything but be slippery.

Verdict: Fine for sex. It was never a treatment and it never said it was.

#4 — Replens

Better in one real way: three days per application instead of twenty minutes.
But here's the manufacturer's own ingredient list. Water, glycerin, mineral oil, polycarbophil, carbomer, palm oil glyceride, methylparaben, sorbic acid, sodium hydroxide.

Glycerin second. Mineral oil third — that's a petroleum derivative. A paraben in there too.

No hyaluronic acid. Nothing for inflammation.

Verdict: Longer-lasting surface moisture, built on the two ingredients I'd most want off that list. 

#3 — VMAGIC Vaginal Suppository

Now we're in the right format. This is a suppository — it stays in contact with the tissue overnight instead of sitting on the surface for twenty minutes. That matters more than most women realize.

It's also honest, which I appreciate. The full ingredient list is: Natural Glycerides of a Vegetable Origin, Sodium Hyaluronate. 5mg of hyaluronic acid per insert. Two ingredients, no hidden anything.

Hyaluronic acid is the right molecule — it binds up to a thousand times its weight in water and draws moisture into the tissue rather than coating it.

But that's the whole formula. Nothing for the inflammation. Nothing supporting the tissue structure. Nothing addressing pH.

Verdict: Right delivery, right molecule, no glycerin. Still solving one problem out of four.

#2 — Revaree

This was the closest competitor to my top pick, and I want to be fair to it. Revaree has genuine clinical work behind it, including head-to-head data against vaginal estrogen for dryness. Correct format, correct molecule, and my patients who use it generally report their dryness improves.

The formula is 5mg hyaluronic acid in semi-synthetic glycerides. The Plus version doubles the HA to 10mg and adds sweet almond oil.

But more hyaluronic acid is still just hyaluronic acid. 

There’s nothing for inflammation, nothing for tissue repair.

And it is FDA-cleared — what it's cleared to do is moisturize and lubricate. That's the claim.

Verdict: A good product doing one thing well. No glycerin here either. Just nothing beyond the basic hydration. 

Nothing for inflammation or burning. 

#1 — Vevival

This is the only product I reviewed that addressed all four problems.

Sodium hyaluronate — hydration held in the tissue. Same molecule as #2 and #3, correct delivery.

Your body makes one molecule whose only job is holding water in that tissue. After menopause, it drops by up to 94%.

One gentle enough for tissue that's already raw. And reaction-free, because my hooha reacts to everything.

This Halloween I carried the cooler. Linda wore short sleeves. It was 20 degrees. Let them look.

Over 100,000 customers. Up to 60 percent off, 30-day guarantee, even on empty pouches. It is not age. It is a gap. Close it.

Five bottles would run you over a hundred dollars a month. One gummy packs all five at 62 cents a day. Over 100,000 customers. Up to 60 percent off, 30 days or every cent back.

A supply line only counts if it keeps running. Stop, and it empties.

Moringa.

Not synthetic hormones.

Just natural support.

It’s built around a potent form of moringa designed for women going through menopause.

The stiffness started easing.

If your joints have been hurting since menopause and nothing has worked, it might not be your joints.

It might be low estrogen.

I can't stand when men tell women period pain is just normal because I'd bet money they couldn't handle how harsh my periods are

I've lost count of how many times I've heard some version of “it's just your period”

Usually from a man who has absolutely no idea what he's talking about

They make it sound like you should take a painkiller, get some sleep and carry on with your day

But my periods weren't like that

Every month, I could practically feel my life coming to a halt

A few days before my period, my energy would start disappearing

I'd wake up tired after a full night's sleep

I'd sit down to answer an email and completely lose my train of thought

I'd have things I needed to get done and somehow couldn't find the energy to do any of them

Then the irritability would hit

The smallest things could set me off

I'd snap at people I cared about and then feel awful about it afterward

And once my period actually started, the heavy bleeding would leave me feeling completely wiped out

It wasn't just a bad day

It was several days of feeling like I had nothing left in the tank

8 years on Nexium for my reflux. Here's what I wish I'd known frоm day one:

My stomach lining was getting thinner the whole time. And no one mentioned it.

I started the pills in my early 50s. Heartburn after every meal. 

That burning in my chest at night. 

Doctor said take Nexium, so I took it.

And it helped. At first.

But over the years, I noticed the burn creeping back. 

Not just heartburn anymore.

🔥 The acid taste pooling in my throat at 2am
🔥 Waking up with a voice like I'd gargled broken glass
🔥 That raw, scraped feeling in my chest that wouldn't quit
🔥 Burping up dinner three hours after I'd eaten it
🔥 The burning so bad some nights I'd sleep sitting up in a chair

I kept a bottle of Tums on my nightstand. Another in my purse. Another in my car.

I knew every gas station bathroom between my house and my daughter's.

I tried everything:

❌ Prilosec when Nexium stopped working
❌ Pepcid on top of the PPI
❌ Gaviscon before bed (chalky and useless)
❌ Apple cider vinegar (burned worse)
❌ Elevating my bed 6 inches (helped a little, husband hated it)
❌ Cutting out coffee, wine, tomatoes, citrus, chocolate (miserable AND still burning)
❌ $200 wedge pillow (slid off it every night)

Nothing worked. Or it worked for a week, then stopped.

I always blamed myself.

Ate too late. Too much coffee. Should've skipped the wine.

I never blamed the pill. Why would I? The doctor said I'd probably need it long-term.

So I kept taking it. 8 years.

My breaking point came at my granddaughter's christening.

Standing in that church, surrounded by family.

The burn started during the ceremony.

That slow creep up my chest. The acid taste in the back of my throat.

I tried to ignore it.

By the time we got to the reception, I was sweating.

I couldn't eat. Couldn't drink. Couldn't hold a conversation.

My daughter asked, "Mom, are you okay?"

I spent the rest of her daughter's christening in the bathroom, splashing water on my face, chewing Tums like candy.

I missed the cake. Missed the photos. Missed my son-in-law's toast.

I drove home in silence, thinking:
I've been on these pills for 8 years. Why is this getting WORSE?

Two weeks later, I was at my daughter's house.

Her mother-in-law Linda was there—a retired gastroenterologist, 70s, sharp as a tack.

We got talking about health stuff and I mentioned I'd been on Nexium forever but still got the burn sometimes.

She put down her tea and looked at me.

"How long have you been on it?"

"Eight years."

"Has anyone explained to you what's actually happening in your stomach?"

I shook my head.

She grabbed a napkin and drew three circles.

"Think of your stomach as a system with three parts that all have to work together. When one breaks down, the others follow. And right now? All three are probably failing."

"PROBLEM #1: The Lining is Thinning"

"Your stomach has a mucus layer—like a raincoat protecting the tissue frоm acid. When you're young, it's thick. But after 50, the cells that make mucus slow down. The lining gets thinner. Worn. Patchy.

PPIs reduce acid—but they don't rebuild the lining. So even a little acid burns straight through the gaps."

"PROBLEM #2: The Tissue is Damaged"

"Once acid gets through the mucus layer, it damages the tissue underneath. Raw. Irritated. Inflamed.

Antacids neutralize acid temporarily—but they don't heal the tissue. It stays damaged. Vulnerable. Every meal is another assault."

Up. Through the valve. Into your esophagus.

You can have a perfectly healed lining, but if food isn't moving, the pressure will push acid up anyway."

"THIS is where you are. Thin lining. Damaged tissue. Stalled digestion. And no pill is fixing all three."

"Why didn't my doctor tell me this?"

Her Package is made from grass-fed, grass-finished beef ovary, uterus, fallopian tubes, liver and kidney from New Zealand cattle, freeze-dried into capsules so the nutrients stay intact.

Her Package brings those foods back in a form that fits into a normal day. There's something my boyfriend used to do in bed that I loved. Two years ago I made him stop, and I let him think it was a preference. Last month I let him again — and the only reason I did was something I ordered at two in the morning, nine weeks before.

Here's what happened. Me and Tom got together when I was 26. I was the girl who walked round the flat in knickers and a t-shirt. I'd sit on his lap while he was trying to work. I'd never once thought about my body as a problem, because it had never been one.

Then at 27 I got a kidney infection. A week of antibiotics, done, back to normal. Except about two weeks later, the day after my period, I stood in the bathroom and thought: what is that?

Not fishy. Everyone says fishy. Mine was more like warm pennies. Strong, and wrong, and coming from me.

The doctor gave me a gel. It worked - brilliant. Two weeks later, back. Another gel. Back. Third time, they swabbed me and it came back fine while I stood there knowing full well it wasn't. The fourth doctor said, "Some women are just like that." I drove home thinking: so this is me now.

And that's when the hiding started. An alarm at 5:40 so I could shower before he woke up. Checking before he got home from work. A spare gel in my washbag - he found it once and I said thrush cream, and that's the closest he's ever come. Getting dressed in the bathroom, door shut, in my own flat.

And in bed - the thing he did that I loved, I made him stop. Told him I'd gone off it. Then sex became something I got through. Lights off. Quick. Then "I'm tired," three nights out of four. He asked me once, on the drive back from his mum's, "Have I done something?" I said no. I let him carry on thinking it was him, because that was easier than the truth. I'd rather he thought I'd gone off him than know why.

I tried everything. Water only. Then not washing at all in case it was that. Boric acid every Sunday night like church. A probiotic off Amazon, £27 a bottle, three months, nothing - if anything, worse. I had a fake account for asking about it online. That's how ashamed I was. I couldn't even put my own name to the question.

That's where I was at 2am on a Tuesday, under a video about BV, reading comments. Hundreds of women asking what I was asking. And one comment - a woman with a sunflower for a profile picture, four paragraphs long - that I read four times.

Here's what she'd written, more or less. Every single thing you've used works by killing. Antibiotics kill. The gel kills. Boric acid kills. Washing kills. But the bacteria behind this don't sit on the surface waiting to be killed. They build a shield- a biofilm, basically a wall they hide behind. Treatment clears everything on top. What's under the wall waits. Then your period comes, and it's back, and you're at the GP being told your swab's fine.

And the bit that made me put my phone down: your body already knows how to deal with this. The good bacteria make lactic acid. Lactic acid keeps you acidic, and acidic keeps everything else out. Every course you've taken wiped out the bad and took the good with it, and nothing you've bought has ever put the good back. You're not dirty. You're empty.

Two years, four doctors, and a stranger with a sunflower explained it in four paragraphs.

She'd named what she took. I ordered it at 2:14 in the morning. Two capsules with my coffee , big, no taste, over in a second. Six strains of the good bacteria, 26 billion of them, with fibre to feed them so they stay, and pineapple enzyme to help break down the wall so they can get in. Not killing anything. Moving the right stuff back in and shutting the door.

Day four, I peeled my leggings off after the gym and stood there sniffing like a lunatic. Nothing. Then my period came and went, and I did what I always do — counted the days to the two-week mark like waiting for a bus. It never came.

Week five, I walked from the bathroom to the bedroom in a towel and dropped it on the floor without thinking. Then noticed I'd done it. Then stood there for a second, because I couldn't remember the last time.

Week seven, I let him. The thing we'd stopped. Lights on. And afterwards he lay there and said, "Where have you been?" And I said, "Here. Just hiding."

But here's the bit you actually need to hear. The moment wasn't in bed. It was a Tuesday morning three weeks before , day fourteen after my period, standing in the bathroom waiting for it the way you wait for bad news, and it didn't come. I stood there and laughed, on my own, at half seven, with the door open. Two years of getting dressed in the bathroom. Now I don't even shut the door.

I spent years buying every arthritis supplement I could find because I was desperate to avoid taking ibuprofen every day.

Collagen. Glucosamine. Fish oil. Turmeric. If someone recommended it, I probably bought it.

Some gave me a little relief, but nothing actually changed. Every morning my joints were still stiff. The stairs still hurt. My hands still ached opening jars.

Then I came across a rheumatologist explaining why.

He rated all the supplements I'd been taking, and honestly it finally made sense.

Collagen wasn't addressing inflammation.

Glucosamine had mixed evidence.

Fish oil wasn't dosed high enough in most products.

Even turmeric wasn't enough because most brands only contain 2-6% curcumin, and curcumin only tackles one part of the inflammation.

The ingredient I'd never even heard of was Boswellia.

It works completely differently to curcumin, which is why taking both together made so much more sense than taking turmeric on its own.

That's why I switched to Nova's Curcumin + Boswellia.

It combines 95% standardized curcumin, full-strength Boswellia and black pepper extract to help absorption.

Within a few weeks I wasn't reaching for ibuprofen every day anymore. My mornings became easier, I was moving better, and my joints finally felt like they were improving instead of getting worse.

If you've tried all the usual arthritis supplements without much success, this combination is honestly worth looking into.

Ever go to bed absolutely wrecked…
but your brain decides it’s the perfect time to start thinking about everything?

Work.
Bills.
That awkward thing you said five years ago.

Next thing you know, it’s 3am.

Here’s something most people don’t realise:

It’s not always stress causing this.

Very often, the body is simply low on magnesium — the mineral responsible for calming the nervous system and helping your body wind down for sleep.

So naturally, many people try magnesium supplements.

But here’s where things go wrong.

Most magnesium tablets absorb very poorly.

A large portion of the mineral passes straight through the digestive system before your body can actually use it.

Which is why many people take magnesium for weeks… and still find themselves staring at the ceiling at night.

Now more people across Ireland are discovering a different approach.

Instead of pills, they’re switching to liquid magnesium drops.

Oriel Sleep Drops contain deep-sea magnesium with trace minerals, designed to absorb far more efficiently than traditional supplements.

Just add a few drops to water about 30 minutes before bed.

No pills.
No bloating.
No complicated routine.

Just a simple way to help your body relax — the way it’s supposed to.

Sometimes better sleep isn’t about trying harder.

It’s about giving your body the mineral it’s been missing.

https://magnesiumstore.com/products/magnesium-for-sleep

The molecule that ends vaginal dryness after menopause was discovered in 1934.

Your gynecologist has never once offered it to you.

It BOILS my blood, because I found it by accident after two years of pain.

I'm not going to walk you through two years of pain. You're living it. You know the burning, the dryness that made lube feel like a joke.

Let me tell you what I found the night I stopped believing I had to live with a dry vagina and painful sex — the night that made me so angry I wrote this post today.

Once you see what it really is, you'll be as angry as I am.

Your body makes one molecule whose only job is holding water in that tissue. After menopause, it drops by up to 94%.

That's it. That's the whole thing.

The vaginal tissue dries from the inside, thins, and tears at the lightest touch. That's the sandpaper. 

That's the blood on the sheets you've been blaming yourself for. Not aging. One molecule, GONE.

And here's the part that made my throat tight in anger.

That molecule isn't rare. It's called hyaluronic acid, and medicine has used it everywhere for ninety years.

Eye surgeons use it. Knee surgeons inject it. It's in the face cream on your shelf right now. Dentists use it to heal the inside of your mouth.

Everywhere on your body. Except the one place menopause was stripping it from.

Not because it was hard. The molecule was right there. They just decided that once you stopped being able to have kids, the rest of you wasn't worth the trouble. So they handed you a tube and told you to cope. 

That's when I understood why nothing I'd tried before was made to heal, and only made my symptoms worse.

For example, the lube doctors recommend only puts water on top of tissue that's dry from the inside. It's like trying to soak a waterproof jacket.

And I thought I could just use  hyaluronic acid, but that molecule is too big to be absorbed by the vaginal tissue.

That's why you need it in the lesser form: sodium hyaluronate.

And OMG, this article I read made me hold my head, because I could not believe it.

In 2023, sodium hyaluronate went head to head with a $1,500 laser treatment for vaginal dryness.

And guess what?

They both had the same result for the two groups of females… that's how POWERFUL this thing is.

And all this time no one said a word\!

A product that treats the symptom keeps you a subscription and a money machine. That's why they never hand off the thing that actually treats the tissue.

But that ends today\!

After sodium hyaluronate brings water back to the vaginal tissue, it doesn't end there.

Because your tissue is torn and you need something to build it back up, which is why you need Centella. Burn units have used it for centuries to rebuild what got thin enough to bleed.

And this is the part that scared me the most and made me anxious.

If the vaginal wall is left torn and untreated, it lets bad bacteria in, causing BV, yeast infections, and leaving us to live on antibiotics forever\!

Third, we need something to calm the burning and protect us from the infection cycle, and that's what chamomile, mallow, and tea tree oil do.

Six ingredients, every one already trusted in real medicine for centuries. They just used them on everyone but us. Burn victims got them. Cancer patients got them. 

And the whole time, the one place menopause was tearing apart got a tube of lube. 

And this is what led me to do more research, to look for a product that actually combines sodium hyaluronate and the other ingredients. 

I looked for one that's hormone-free, because cancer runs in my family. 

One gentle enough for tissue that's already raw. And reaction-free, because my hooha reacts to everything.

So I found a suppository, inserted inside the vagina to target the actual tissue.

Because I knew pills don't work — the stomach acid destroys them before they reach the tissue — and topical creams don't get absorbed.

I have never had something work on me the way this did.

* Week one: the burning when I peed stopped because the tissue was rebuilt. That stretching, splitting feeling every time I moved, gone.

* Day twenty: moisture I hadn't felt in three years, and sex I'd forgotten the feeling of. I cried after.

Her name was Dr Elena Voss.

Studying the actual tissue.

She wanted to know what this tissue actually was. What does it need? And why does it fall apart when other tissue in the body doesn't?

Nobody would fund the question. So she answered it herself.

After-hours lab time. Weekends. Tissue samples from surgical departments that were going to throw them in the trash.

She started testing. If vaginal tissue breaks down after menopause, what other tissue in the body behaves the same way? What other membrane heals the same way?

She needed a match.

Esophageal tissue. Close. Not close enough.

Nasal. No.

Intestinal. No.

Rectal. Closer. Still not right.

Months of testing. Months of nothing matching.

Then one night - late, alone in the lab, running one more comparison before going home — she tested vaginal tissue against oral mucosa.

The tissue inside the mouth. The inner cheek..

She ran it twice because she didn't believe the first result.

They weren't similar.

They were identical.

Same cells. Same layers. Same thickness. Same way of absorbing things. Same way of breaking down. Same way of healing.

The tissue inside your vagina and the tissue inside your mouth are the same tissue.

She sat in that lab for a long time. 

Because if that was true — if those tissues heal the same way, break down the same way, absorb compounds the same way — then anything that heals one should heal the other.

Anything that works inside your mouth should work inside your vagina. Because it's the same membrane.

Paris, 1767. The first restaurants did not open to serve croissants. They opened to feed weak people a strange tea brewed from meat. That is where the word comes from. Restaurant. To restore.

A few days in, the muscles fill back with water. Then it hardens. Saturday only costs you Saturday. The guy you were at 35 is back.

A lab tested 12 brands and half came up short. Bear Balanced came in over its label. Creapure, 99 percent pure, made under pharma standards in Germany. More than 100,000 people already take it.
